family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with alternate simple leaves and tiny axillary flowers, then confirm a superior ovary maturing into a drupe with several pyrenes.
family_diagnostics.habit: Woody shrubs/trees; local set spans deciduous possumhaw and evergreen yaupon.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Tiny mostly 4–5-merous unisexual flowers; plants usually dioecious.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Small drupe with several hard pyrenes, not a true botanical berry.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Red fruit alone is not enough—leaf texture and deciduous/evergreen habit matter.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: The holly lesson is mostly about separating leaf/habit types while keeping the same tiny-flower → multi-pyrene drupe architecture.

steps.title: 1 · Deciduous possumhaw
steps.look_for: Leafless winter twigs loaded with red/orange drupes.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows the deciduous exception inside a family many people assume is evergreen.

steps.title: 2 · Evergreen yaupon fruit
steps.look_for: Tiny leathery evergreen leaves with persistent red drupes.

steps.title: 3 · Learn flower sex
steps.image_credit: Public Domain · USGS / Helen Lowe Metzman
steps.look_for: Tiny flower with functional ovary and reduced staminodes.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains why only female plants fruit in dioecious hollies.

steps.title: 4 · Nursery-trade comparison
steps.image_credit: Public Domain · USGS / Helen Lowe Metzman
steps.look_for: Functional stamens and a reduced pistillode.
steps.why_it_matters: Provides a male-flower comparison while retaining I. opaca as a non-target-zone native comparison only.

comparisons.title: Aquifoliaceae vs Ebenaceae
comparisons.rule: Ilex has small drupes with several pyrenes and tiny axillary flowers; Diospyros has larger berries with a conspicuous persistent calyx.

comparisons.title: Possumhaw vs yaupon
comparisons.rule: Possumhaw is deciduous with larger thinner leaves; yaupon is evergreen with tiny leathery crenate leaves.

visual_lesson.caveat: American holly remains a comparison taxon and should not be counted in project-native metrics.
